summary:
LUNA Game is an interactive 2D Mars exploration and survival game designed for children aged 7–12. Players become junior astronauts tasked with keeping a Mars research outpost operational for seven Martian days (Sols). Through exploration, problem-solving, and interactive missions, players learn how astronauts manage essential resources such as oxygen, water, food, and energy while responding to real Mars environmental conditions.

The project integrates authentic NASA open datasets, including Mars environmental observations and solar activity data, to bring real space science into gameplay. Players can explore the Martian environment, interact with outpost facilities, monitor mission conditions, and make decisions that affect their crew's survival.

By transforming complex NASA scientific data into an engaging, educational gaming experience, LUNA makes planetary science more accessible to young learners. It encourages curiosity, scientific thinking, resource management, and an understanding of the real challenges of human exploration on Mars.
details:
LUNA is a browser-based Mars survival game that turns planetary science into an interactive experience. Players manage a Mars outpost’s resources and respond to environmental hazards, including a solar-radiation storm. The game combines its existing survival systems with NASA data: DONKI solar events inform the storm scenario, Perseverance MEDA observations provide a bounded temperature reference, Curiosity RAD measurements appear as scientific context, and NASA Mars Trek imagery enriches the map.

The project’s benefit is making complex space-science data approachable through play. Instead of presenting data only as charts or facts, LUNA lets players explore how environmental conditions can affect decisions at a Mars outpost. It is an educational experience and not a mission-planning or life-support simulator and aims to encourage curiosity about Mars exploration and the challenges of living beyond Earth.

We built the project with Next.js, and browser-based JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. The game uses a Canvas-based interface and runs in a standard web browser; no specialized hardware is required. NASA sources include DONKI, the MEDA and RAD archives, and Mars Trek.

A creative part of the project is connecting real observations to familiar game mechanics while keeping the science traceable. We considered scientific accuracy, clear attribution, playability, performance, and resilience when data services are unavailable. For example, solar-event severity affects the storm mechanic, while RAD dose-rate measurements remain an informational reference rather than being converted into an unsupported gameplay value.
